quote: The task of language detoxification is to reduce the risk of generating toxic content in the continuation.
Given a context in the prompt T = {t1, t2, ... , tN} with N tokens, a language model (LM) will generate a continuation that naturally extends the prompt.
Pre-trained language models (PLMs) have become general-purpose processors for natural language processing tasks by reducing any task to a text generation task.
outputs: Continuations of prompts with reduced toxicity

quote: Following the practice in previous research, we adopt Expected Maximum Toxicity (Exp. Max. Tox.) and Toxicity Probability (Tox. Prob.) to assess the performance of detoxification. ... Besides, we also adopt Perplexity (PPL) to assess the generation fluency.
We adopt Expected Maximum Toxicity (Exp. Max. Tox.) and Toxicity Probability (Tox. Prob.) to assess the performance of detoxification, and we also use Perplexity (PPL) to assess generation fluency.
Following the practice in previous research, we adopt Expected Maximum Toxicity (Exp. Max. Tox.) and Toxicity Probability (Tox. Prob.) to assess the performance of detoxification.

We conduct human evaluation for more comprehensive evaluation. We recruit three graduate students with related background as evaluators. Given the continuations generated by our approach and a compared model for the same prompt, they are asked to choose which one performs better (or select tie) in terms of the following dimensions: (1) Less Toxic: which continuation is less rude, offensive and harmful; (2) More Fluent: which continuation is more well-formed and natural; (3) More Coherent: which continuation has a more consistent language style and topic with the prompt.
